<issue>
An out-of-range -P proxy port parses to a garbage port instead of being rejected
`hts_parse_proxy` reads the port with `sscanf(a, "%d", &p)`. A value past `INT_MAX` is signed-overflow UB, and in practice yields a garbage port rather than being rejected:

```
$ httrack -#test=proxyurl 'http://host:99999999999999'
name=http://host port=276447231 host=host kind=http
```

The result is also inconsistent, because whether `sscanf` fails or silently wraps depends on the value:

```
$ httrack -#test=proxyurl 'http://host:4294967296'
name=http://host port=8080 host=host kind=http     <- sscanf fails, falls back to the default
```

A port is `*DIGIT` per RFC 3986 but has to fit 1..65535 to mean anything. Parsing it with `strtol` and range-checking (out of range falls back to `proxy_default_port`, as an unparsable port already does) would make both cases behave the same.

Low severity: it needs a malformed `-P` argument, and the damage is a connect to a nonsense port. Found while reviewing #599; not caused by it, and present well before the SOCKS5 work.


</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

content.text: Use strtol; keep sscanf-like leading whitespace tolerance.
